briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East situation remains highly volatile with significant escalation in the Strait of Hormuz, where US forces disabled Iranian oil tankers and Iran retaliated with a claimed missile-drone attack on US destroyers. Concurrently, the Israel-Lebanon border experienced intensified hostilities with Hezbollah launching explosive drone attacks that wounded three Israeli soldiers, met by extensive Israeli airstrikes on over 85 Hezbollah targets. The UAE also reported intercepting Iranian missile and drone attacks, resulting in three injuries.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran include the US military disabling two Iranian oil tankers, "Sea Star III" and "Sevda," near Iranian ports with an F/A-18 Super Hornet, and a third tanker, "Hasna," previously stopped. The Iranian Navy claims to have launched a combined missile-drone operation (8 cruise missiles, 24 suicide drones) on May 8 against three US destroyers in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming hits and fires. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned US actions as ceasefire violations. Iran is broadcasting warnings to vessels to maintain a 10-mile distance from US warships in the Strait. US CENTCOM reports stopping over 70 tankers since the naval blockade began, amounting to over 166 million barrels of oil. US Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and companies from China and Hong Kong for aiding Iran's Shahed drone program, and 3 individuals and 9 companies from Belarus and China for WMD proliferation. A spokesperson for Iran's Khatam HQ stated Iran will not negotiate from weakness and threatened "gates of hell" if dialogue closes. An Iranian military source indicates current clashes in the Persian Gulf have halted but could resume if US forces return. Mohammad Mokhber, an advisor to the Leader, asserted the Strait of Hormuz offers "atomic bomb-sized" capability to influence the global economy. Iran also seized the oil tanker "Ocean Koi" in the Gulf of Oman.

Internally, US intelligence (CNN) assesses Mojtaba Khamenei is deeply involved in decision-making, though difficult to track due to his avoidance of electronic communication. An official from the Leader's office stated Mojtaba Khamenei sustained minor injuries (knee, back, behind ear) during the bombing of the Leader's house, where his wife was killed, contradicting earlier reports of severe burns. The Judiciary Chief warned against underestimating "foot soldiers" (those spreading rumors). President Pezeshkian reaffirmed Iran's commitment to friendly relations and anti-colonialism. Rallies supporting the leadership and armed forces were held nationwide.

Economically, OPEC reported a decrease in members' oil revenue for 2025, with Iran earning over $45 billion (6th highest). Al-Jazeera reported that Americans paid an additional $40 billion for gas over the past two months due to the Strait of Hormuz closure. The price of gold increased by 2.3% this week, linked to optimism about Iran-US negotiations. An oil spill near Kharg Island was reported by AP, while an Iranian official denied Iranian responsibility, blaming a European tanker. The European Aviation Agency noted impacts on jet fuel supplies due to the Middle East situation.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations were extensive, with the IDF striking over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, rocket launchers, buildings, and an underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley. The Israeli Air Force targeted a rocket launcher used in a recent barrage on the Western Galilee and Haifa Bay. An interceptor missile was fired at a suspected Hezbollah drone over southern Lebanon, with results under review. The IDF is preparing for potential renewed rocket fire from Lebanon into northern Israel. In Gaza, the IDF's Brigade 12 completed its mission in the southern Gaza Strip, destroying 8 Hamas underground tunnels and terror infrastructure in eastern Rafah.

Casualties include three Israeli soldiers wounded by Hezbollah explosive drones; one seriously, and two moderately. One incident occurred in Israeli territory near the border, the other near troops in southern Lebanon. On the home front, Hezbollah fired several rockets at the Western Galilee and Haifa Bay area; one was intercepted, and others fell in open areas with no injuries reported, though sirens sounded in Qiryat and Acre. A Hezbollah drone was discovered on a school roof in Nahariya, prompting police to secure the area.

Politically, PM Netanyahu defended his appointment of Roman Gofman as Mossad head to the High Court, asserting the PM's sole responsibility for national security decisions. Israeli Channel 12 reported that Israel is on full alert for renewed war with Iran, conveying to the US that any war resumption should include the destruction of Iran's energy infrastructure within 24 hours. The credit rating agency S&P maintained Israel's credit rating at A/A-1 with a stable outlook.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In ground operations, the IDF completed its mission in southern Gaza, destroying 8 Hamas underground tunnels and terror infrastructure in eastern Rafah. Residents of the al-Shati refugee camp in Gaza City were forced to sleep on the streets following Israeli attacks, and an Israeli airstrike hit a residential building in the camp. In the West Bank, settlers reportedly forced Palestinians to exhume a body from a grave and moved it, an action condemned by the IDF. Separately, settlers were observed digging in a Palestinian cemetery in Fandaqumiya (Samaria), leaving upon the arrival of forces. An Israeli settler deliberately blocked a Palestinian ambulance in southern Nablus, and armed Israeli soldiers forced Palestinians out of Deir Balut, western Salfit. Casualties include Dr. Hussam Abu Safia, director of Kamal Adwan Hospital, who reportedly suffered systematic torture in Israeli prison. The humanitarian situation saw Palestinians participate in the 10th Palestine International Marathon in central Gaza. Iran (per Press TV) is reported to seek a "permanent ceasefire" in Gaza.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations included firing several rockets at the Western Galilee and Haifa Bay area, one of which was intercepted while others fell in open areas, causing no injuries. Sirens sounded in Qiryat and Acre. Hezbollah also launched explosive drones, wounding three Israeli soldiers (one seriously, two moderately); one drone exploded in Israeli territory near the border, and others near troops in southern Lebanon. A Hezbollah drone was found on a school roof in Nahariya. Hezbollah claimed to have disabled a Merkava tank with a guided missile in Taybeh, southern Lebanon, and burned two Merkava tanks in Al-Bayada and one at the Nimr Al-Jabal site. The group also claimed targeting a "Nimera" vehicle in Bint Jbeil with suicidal drones on May 1 and May 2.

In response, Israeli strikes were extensive, with the IDF hitting over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, rocket launchers, and buildings. An underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley was also struck. Israeli airstrikes were reported in Ayta Aljabal (southern Lebanon), Beqaa (eastern Lebanon, including Brital and Khuraybah outskirts), Tura (southern Lebanon), Deir Aames (southern Lebanon), and Al-Siad (southern Lebanon). The IDF Arabic spokesperson issued an evacuation warning for residents in southern Lebanon near Hezbollah activities, advising them to move 1 km away.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, a government committee is reportedly preparing a plan to disarm pro-Iranian militias, which will be presented to the Trump administration. Explosions were heard in Sulaymaniyah and Erbil provinces, northern Iraq, attributed to a drone attack on Iranian opposition parties. The Iraqi National Security Service announced a significant operation against banned Ba'ath party formations, infiltrating their online activities and leading to arrests of leaders and members. A bomb explosion in Hīt, Iraq, wounded two people. Militarily, Russia's Africa Corps, alongside the Mali army, launched a new offensive against Al-Qaeda jihadist forces. A US Air Force Bombardier E-11A was observed flying over Iraq, providing communications support.

GULF STATES
The UAE Ministry of Defense announced intercepting five new missile and drone attacks, consisting of two missiles and three drones, which resulted in three injuries. Kuwait reduced marine boat traffic due to fears of Iranian attacks. Diplomatically, Saudi Arabia denied reports of opening its airspace for US military aggression against Iran, calling such claims suspicious. A Saudi diplomatic source indicated that negotiations on the nuclear program and Strait of Hormuz are difficult and slow. Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister met with US Vice President Pence in Washington to discuss regional developments and Pakistan's mediation efforts. Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov and Saudi Foreign Minister Ben Farhan discussed the Strait of Hormuz and emphasized the need to normalize Iran-Arab Gulf relations. An Emirati influencer, Amjad Taha, issued a stern warning to Iran, emphasizing the UAE's strength and independence from Western powers. The US approved $17 billion in missile sales to Kuwait, UAE, and Bahrain. The economic impact on the region includes a report by Middle East Eye that the war against Iran has caused a sharp decline in tourism in Dubai, devastating its hotel industry. The UAE is also reported to be funding a US- and Israel-backed police force for Gaza. Leaders of ASEAN expressed "serious concern" over the changing Middle East situation and called for freedom of navigation.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Direct US-Iran Confrontations in Strait of Hormuz:** The US military reported disabling two Iranian oil tankers, "Sea Star III" and "Sevda," and a previous one, "Hasna." Iran's military claimed a retaliatory missile-drone operation (8 cruise missiles, 24 suicide drones) against three US destroyers, asserting hits and fires.
2.  **Strait of Hormuz Closure:** No commercial vessels run by registered shipping companies have crossed the Strait of Hormuz since Tuesday, with US CENTCOM reporting over 70 tankers stopped, impacting global oil supplies and reportedly costing Americans $40 billion in increased gas prices.
3.  **Hezbollah Drone Attacks on Israel:** Three Israeli soldiers were wounded (one seriously, two moderately) by Hezbollah explosive drones, one of which exploded in Israeli territory near the border. A Hezbollah drone was also found on the roof of a school in Nahariya.
4.  **Extensive Israeli Strikes in Lebanon:** The IDF struck over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon, including an underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley, in response to continued aggression.
5.  **UAE Intercepts Iranian Missile/Drone Attacks:** The UAE Ministry of Defense reported intercepting five new Iranian missile and drone attacks, resulting in three injuries.
6.  **Mojtaba Khamenei's Injuries and Influence:** US intelligence assesses Mojtaba Khamenei's critical role in Iranian decision-making. An Iranian official detailed his injuries (knee, back, behind ear) sustained during a bombing of the Leader's house, where his wife was killed.
7.  **US-Iran Ceasefire and Negotiations:** US President Trump stated he expects Iran's response to a peace proposal soon, warning of a "Freedom Plus" project in the Strait of Hormuz if no agreement is reached. Iran's Foreign Ministry indicated its response is still under review.
8.  **Russia-Ukraine 3-Day Ceasefire:** US President Trump announced a 3-day ceasefire (May 9-11) between Russia and Ukraine, which both nations confirmed, and includes an exchange of 2000 prisoners (1000 from each side).

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high in the Strait of Hormuz due to direct US-Iran military confrontations and explicit Iranian warnings of a "decisive response" if US forces re-enter or disturb Iranian vessels. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi suggests US "military adventurism" sacrifices diplomacy, while an Israeli report indicates Israel is on "full alert" for war with Iran, with a focus on destroying its energy infrastructure. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz (US-Iran naval engagement, Iranian warnings to shipping), the Israel-Lebanon border (Hezbollah drone and rocket attacks met with extensive Israeli responses, with the IDF preparing for further escalation), and the UAE (recent Iranian missile/drone attacks causing injuries). Military posture changes involve Israel on "full alert" for war with Iran, the US CENTCOM enforcing a naval blockade in Hormuz, and the Iranian Navy seizing tankers and issuing warnings. The US is also supplying Gulf states with advanced missiles. Red lines include the US warning that if Americans are threatened, they will be "destroyed," and Iran's assertion that control over Hormuz is an "atomic bomb-sized capability."

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture includes President Trump's declared desire to end the war with Iran and his expectation of an Iranian response to a peace proposal, with a warning of a "Freedom Plus" project in the Strait of Hormuz if negotiations fail. Secretary of State Rubio clarified that recent US actions in Hormuz were "defensive" responses to Iranian fire, distinct from the "Epic Fury" offensive, and reiterated the US "red line" against threats to Americans. The US also announced sanctions against Chinese and Belarusian entities for aiding Iran's drone and WMD programs and approved $17 billion in missile sales to Kuwait, UAE, and Bahrain. US VP Pence met with Qatar's PM/FM to discuss regional developments and Pakistan's mediation.

Among Gulf States, Saudi Arabia denied allowing its airspace for US aggression against Iran. Saudi FM Ben Farhan discussed the Strait of Hormuz with Russian FM Lavrov, stressing normalization of Iran-Arab Gulf relations. The UAE intercepted Iranian missile/drone attacks, resulting in three injuries, and Kuwait reduced marine traffic fearing Iranian attacks. Qatar's PM/FM discussed mediation with the US.

EU members are considering talks with Russia on May 27-28 and are investigating airlines for "fuel surcharges" due to the conflict. Spanish PM Sánchez was honored for documenting Gaza violations, while protesters in Seville called to cut ties with Israel. Russia confirmed agreement to a 3-day ceasefire with Ukraine (May 9-11) proposed by Trump, including a prisoner exchange. Russia's Foreign Ministry expressed regret over an Israeli company's decision to avoid Russian grain and stated it would not support a US-Bahrain draft resolution against Iran. China is impacted by US sanctions related to Iran's drone program, but Iran's ambassador to China noted that Iran-China relations are expected to deepen. Iran's FM Araghchi also spoke with Turkish FM Fidan about regional insecurity.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions were observed: the severity of Mojtaba Khamenei's injuries is disputed, with one Iranian source detailing minor injuries and his wife's death, while other reports indicated severe burns. Iran's missile reserves are reported by the CIA (via PressTV) as 70% remaining, but Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi claims 120% capacity. The cause of an oil spill near Kharg Island is debated, with AP citing potential infrastructure collapse or deliberate dumping, and an Iranian official blaming a European tanker. The descriptions of naval engagements in the Strait of Hormuz differ significantly, with the US reporting disabling Iranian tankers and Iran claiming successful missile-drone hits on US destroyers. The exact nature and mutual understanding of a "ceasefire" between the US and Iran are also unclear, with Iran citing "violations" and US officials framing actions as "defensive responses."

Unverified claims include specific details on Mojtaba Khamenei's injuries and his wife's death from an internal Iranian source. Iran's claims of hitting US destroyers lack external corroboration in this feed. Al-Jazeera's report on increased US gas costs due to Hormuz is attributed. A report from Channel 12 Israel regarding Israel's intention to destroy Iran's energy infrastructure within 24 hours is a significant and unverified claim.

Propaganda indicators are evident in both US and Iranian statements. Iranian sources frequently emphasize military capabilities, resilience, and US "lawlessness," while US statements highlight strength, "defensive" actions, and determination. The term "Ramadan war" used by an Iranian source, and the UAE influencer's strong rhetoric, also serve as propaganda.

Reporting gaps include a lack of independent confirmation on claimed hits on US destroyers, limited details on UAE casualties from Iranian attacks, and the precise timing of a Hezbollah drone found on a school roof. The specifics of the US "Epic Fury" offensive are not fully detailed, and information regarding an "intermediary Pakistani" for US-Iran negotiations remains vague.
